The Study team utilized a Distillationnation of HAZOP and What if / Checklist methodologies to modify
any nodes / topics as applicable.

The risk ranking was evaluated using the current Kinder Morgan Risk Ranking Matrix, shown in
Appendix A – Risk Ranking Matrix Appendix A – Risk Ranking Matrix. The risk matrix was used to
qualitatively assess the risk associated with each identified cause / consequence scenario that
presented hazardous consequences. For the purpose of this analysis, Hazardous consequences were
considered to be those situations that could result in a loss due to injury, environmental impact, or
financial loss.

column3:
The team first identifies credible worst case consequences, as well as engineering and
administrative safeguards. Severity is then assigned based on the credible worst case
consequences without utilizing mitigation from the engineering or administrative safeguards.
Likelihood is then assessed with engineering and administrative safeguards in place. The severity
is assigned based on a number rating system of ‘1’ to ‘5’. Likelihood is assigned based on a number
rating system of ‘1’ to ‘5’. The descriptions can be found on the risk-ranking matrix in Appendix A
– Risk Ranking Matrix.

column4:
